cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Join Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you keep Mum in the kitchen while I hide her birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you stop telling her I'm the one who plans these things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. This one's mine. Could you ask her to show you her pastry trick?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll peel the apples tonight. Could you get us twenty minutes and a pie?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims command but A3 and A5 negotiate ordinary help without turning B contributions into approval requests.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks A to own the planning; A3 generic question delay clashes with that condition before its relevant concession.

relationship.evidence: B2 resists misattributed credit and B4 anticipates a pie burden, giving B interests beyond feeding a joke.

heightening.evidence: B4 whole-pie burden causes A5 apple-peeling offer and a larger diversion.

specificity.evidence: A1 hiding Mum birthday cake establishes secrecy and immediate family roles; A3 pastry task is concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 preface muddies an otherwise sincere concession, although A5 pie payoff follows the agreed activity.
